title: ICSE CLASS 9 — Social Science | Physical Features India Mountains
description: Subject-wise test on Physical Features India Mountains (Social Science) for ICSE CLASS 9. 25Q.
subject: icse9-sst

questions.question: Which of the following is the highest peak in the Indian Himalayas?

options.explanation: Mount Everest is the highest peak in the world but lies in Nepal, not entirely within the Indian Himalayas.
Nanda Devi is a prominent peak in the Himalayas but not the highest in the Indian Himalayas.
Kanchenjunga is the highest peak located entirely within the Indian Himalayas (Sikkim).
K2 is the highest peak in India but lies in the Karakoram range, not the Himalayas.

questions.explanation: While K2 (Godwin Austin) is the highest peak in India, it lies in the Karakoram range, which is part of the Trans-Himalayan region. Kanchenjunga is the highest peak located entirely within the Indian Himalayas (specifically, Sikkim). Mount Everest is in Nepal.
questions.hint: Consider the location of each peak within the Himalayan ranges.
questions.subject: icse9-sst

questions.question: The longitudinal valleys lying between the Lesser Himalayas (Himachal) and the Shivaliks are known as:

options.explanation: Bhangars are older alluvial plains found in the northern plains, not valleys between Himalayan ranges.
Duns are the longitudinal valleys between the Lesser Himalayas and the Shivaliks.
Khadars are newer alluvial plains found in river valleys, not Himalayan valleys.
Bhabars are the foothill plains of the Himalayas, not the valleys between ranges.

questions.explanation: Duns are the local name for the elongated valleys formed due to the deposition of sediments by rivers flowing from the Himalayas, found between the Lesser Himalayas and the Shivalik range. Examples include Dehradun, Kotli Dun, and Patli Dun.
questions.hint: Think of the valleys formed between the middle and outer Himalayan ranges.
questions.subject: icse9-sst

questions.question: Which of the following mountain ranges is known as the 'Greater Himalayas' or 'Inner Himalayas'?

options.explanation: Himadri is the correct name for the Greater or Inner Himalayas.
Himachal is the Lesser Himalayas, not the Greater Himalayas.
Shivaliks are the Outer Himalayas, not the Greater Himalayas.
Purvanchal refers to the eastern Himalayan ranges, not the Greater Himalayas.

questions.explanation: The Himadri range is the northernmost and most continuous range of the Himalayas, characterized by its highest peaks and perpetual snow cover, hence also known as the Greater or Inner Himalayas.
questions.hint: Consider the alternative names for the Himalayan ranges.
questions.subject: icse9-sst

questions.question: The Himalayas are considered 'young fold mountains' primarily because:

options.text: They are covered with young forests.
options.explanation: The presence of young forests does not define the geological age of mountains.

options.text: They are still growing in height.
options.explanation: While the Himalayas are still growing, this alone does not classify them as young fold mountains.

options.text: They were formed recently by the collision of tectonic plates.
options.explanation: The Himalayas were formed by the collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates, making them young fold mountains.
The age of rocks does not solely determine the classification of mountains as young fold mountains.

questions.explanation: The Himalayas were formed relatively recently in geological terms (around 50-70 million years ago) due to the collision of the Indian plate with the Eurasian plate, causing the Earth's crust to fold and uplift. This process is still ongoing, leading to their classification as young fold mountains.
questions.hint: Consider the geological age and formation process of the Himalayas.
questions.subject: icse9-sst

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic feature of the Shivalik range?

options.text: It is the outermost range of the Himalayas.
options.explanation: The Shivaliks are indeed the outermost range of the Himalayas.

options.text: It is composed of unconsolidated sediments.
options.explanation: The Shivaliks are composed of unconsolidated sediments, making them prone to erosion.

options.text: It has an average height of 6000 metres.
options.explanation: The Shivaliks have an average height of 900 to 1100 metres, not 6000 metres.

options.text: It is prone to earthquakes and landslides.
options.explanation: The Shivaliks are prone to earthquakes and landslides due to their unconsolidated sediments.

questions.explanation: The Shivaliks, or Outer Himalayas, have an average height ranging from 900 to 1100 metres, not 6000 metres. The Himadri (Greater Himalayas) has an average height of over 6000 metres.
questions.hint: Consider the average height of the Shivalik range compared to other Himalayan ranges.
questions.subject: icse9-sst

questions.question: Arrange the following Himalayan ranges from North to South: 1. Shivaliks 2. Himadri 3. Himachal (Lesser Himalayas)

options.explanation: The correct order is Himadri (2), Himachal (3), and Shivaliks (1).
This order is incorrect as it starts with the outermost range.
This order is incorrect as it places the Lesser Himalayas before the Greater Himalayas.
This order is incorrect as it places the Shivaliks before the Lesser Himalayas.

questions.explanation: The correct order from North to South is: Himadri (Greater Himalayas), followed by Himachal (Lesser Himalayas), and then the Shivaliks (Outer Himalayas).
questions.hint: Visualize the Himalayan ranges from north to south based on their geographical position.
questions.subject: icse9-sst

questions.question: A significant impact of the Himalayan ranges on India's climate is that they:

options.text: Cause heavy rainfall throughout the year in the entire country.
options.explanation: The Himalayas do not cause uniform heavy rainfall throughout the year in the entire country.

options.text: Prevent the monsoon winds from reaching Central Asia.
options.explanation: The Himalayas do not prevent monsoon winds from reaching Central Asia; they block cold winds from Central Asia.

options.text: Act as a barrier against cold winds from Central Asia and cause orographic rainfall.
options.explanation: The Himalayas block cold winds from Central Asia and cause orographic rainfall by forcing monsoon winds to rise and shed moisture.

options.text: Facilitate the entry of tropical cyclones into the subcontinent.
options.explanation: The Himalayas do not facilitate the entry of tropical cyclones; they act as a barrier.

questions.explanation: The Himalayas play a crucial role by blocking the extremely cold winds blowing from Central Asia, protecting the Indian subcontinent from severe winters. They also force the moisture-laden monsoon winds to shed their moisture on the Indian side, leading to significant orographic rainfall.
questions.hint: Consider the role of the Himalayas in influencing India's climate patterns.
questions.subject: icse9-sst

questions.question: Assertion (A): The Himadri range is almost continuous. Reason (R): It is composed of highly compressed and altered rocks. Which of the following is correct?

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Reason R is incorrect as the Himadri is not composed of highly compressed and altered rocks.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Reason R is incorrect, so this option is invalid.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Assertion A is correct, but Reason R is incorrect.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: Assertion A is correct, so this option is invalid.

questions.explanation: Assertion A is true; the Himadri (Greater Himalayas) is indeed the most continuous range. However, Reason R is false. The Himadri is composed of granite, not highly compressed and altered rocks, which are more characteristic of the Himachal (Lesser Himalayas).
questions.hint: The Himadri range is known for its continuity, but its rock composition is different from what is stated in Reason R.
questions.subject: icse9-sst

questions.question: A geographer is studying a region in the Himalayas known for its rugged mountains, beautiful hill stations like Shimla and Manali, and extensive longitudinal valleys. Which of the following ranges is he most likely focusing on?

options.explanation: The Trans-Himalayan Range is located north of the main Himalayan ranges and is not known for hill stations.
The Himadri (Greater Himalayas) is too high and rugged for extensive hill stations.
The Himachal range is known for its rugged mountains, hill stations, and longitudinal valleys.
The Purvanchal Hills are located in the eastern part of India and are not associated with hill stations like Shimla and Manali.

questions.explanation: The Himachal, or Lesser Himalayas, is famous for its rugged mountains, popular hill stations like Shimla, Manali, Kullu, and Kangra, and is characterized by the presence of longitudinal valleys (like the Kashmir Valley).
questions.hint: The region described includes popular hill stations and longitudinal valleys.
questions.subject: icse9-sst

questions.question: The 'Purvanchal' mountain range in the east is composed mainly of strong sandstones and extends along the eastern boundary of India. Which of the following is a prominent hill range within the Purvanchal?

options.explanation: The Pir Panjal Range is part of the Lesser Himalayas in the northwest.
The Dhauladhar Range is part of the Lesser Himalayas in the northwest.
The Zaskar Range is part of the Trans-Himalayas in the northwest.
The Naga Hills are a prominent hill range within the Purvanchal.

questions.explanation: The Purvanchal, or Eastern Hills, comprises several hill ranges like the Patkai Bum, Naga Hills, Manipur Hills, and Mizo Hills. The Pir Panjal, Dhauladhar, and Zaskar ranges are part of the main Himalayan system in the north and northwest of India.
questions.hint: The Purvanchal range is located in the eastern part of India and includes several hill ranges.
questions.subject: icse9-sst

questions.question: Which of the following is considered the highest peak in India, including the disputed territories?

options.explanation: Mount Everest is the highest peak in the world but lies in Nepal, not entirely in India.
K2 is the highest peak in the Karakoram range, part of the Indian subcontinent's mountain system.
Kangchenjunga is the highest peak located entirely within India but is not the highest in disputed territories.
Nanda Devi is a prominent peak in India but not the highest.

questions.explanation: K2 (Mount Godwin Austen) is the highest peak in the Karakoram range, located in Gilgit-Baltistan, a territory administered by Pakistan but claimed by India. Geographically, it is part of the Indian subcontinent's mountain system. Kangchenjunga is the highest peak located entirely within India.
questions.hint: Consider peaks in disputed territories as well.
questions.subject: icse9-sst

questions.question: The northernmost and most continuous range of the Himalayas, characterized by its lofty peaks with an average height of 6,000 metres, is known as:

options.explanation: Himadri is the correct term for the northernmost and most continuous range of the Himalayas.
Himachal refers to the Lesser Himalayas.
Shivaliks are the southernmost and youngest range of the Himalayas.
Purvachal refers to the eastern Himalayas.

questions.explanation: The Himadri, also known as the Greater Himalayas, is the innermost and highest range of the Himalayas, featuring the highest peaks and a continuous alignment.
questions.hint: This range is also called the Greater Himalayas.
questions.subject: icse9-sst

questions.question: Which of the following mountain ranges is primarily composed of unconsolidated sediments, gravel, and alluvium brought down by rivers from the main Himalayan ranges?

options.explanation: Greater Himalayas are composed of hard rocks and are the highest range.
Lesser Himalayas are composed of metamorphic and sedimentary rocks.
Shivaliks are composed of unconsolidated sediments and alluvium.
Trans-Himalayas are located north of the Greater Himalayas and are composed of different rock types.

questions.explanation: The Shivaliks, or Outer Himalayas, are the southernmost and youngest range, formed by the deposition of sediments carried by rivers from the higher Himalayan ranges.
questions.hint: This range is also known as the Outer Himalayas.
questions.subject: icse9-sst

questions.question: The Himalayas are often referred to as 'young fold mountains' primarily because:

options.text: They are composed entirely of igneous rocks.
options.explanation: The Himalayas are composed of a variety of rocks, including sedimentary and metamorphic.

options.text: They are still undergoing uplift due to ongoing tectonic plate collision.
options.explanation: The Himalayas are still rising due to the collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates.

options.text: Their peaks are highly eroded and show signs of ancient formation.
options.explanation: The Himalayas are relatively young and not highly eroded.

options.text: They were formed by massive volcanic eruptions.
options.explanation: The Himalayas were formed by tectonic plate collisions, not volcanic activity.

questions.explanation: The term 'young fold mountains' signifies that the Himalayas are geologically recent formations, still actively rising due to the continuous collision of the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates, causing the folding of sedimentary rocks.
questions.hint: Consider the geological age and ongoing tectonic activity.
questions.subject: icse9-sst

questions.question: The regional division of the Himalayas lying between the Satluj and Kali rivers is traditionally known as the:

options.explanation: Punjab Himalayas lie between the Indus and Satluj rivers.
Kumaon Himalayas lie between the Satluj and Kali rivers.
Nepal Himalayas lie between the Kali and Tista rivers.
Assam Himalayas lie between the Tista and Brahmaputra rivers.

questions.explanation: Based on regional divisions from west to east, the segment of the Himalayas located between the Satluj and Kali rivers is referred to as the Kumaon Himalayas.
questions.hint: This division is named after a region in Uttarakhand.
questions.subject: icse9-sst

questions.question: **Assertion (A):** The Northern Plains of India are highly fertile and productive for agriculture. **Reason (R):** The Himalayas act as a climatic barrier, preventing cold winds from Central Asia and causing orographic rainfall on the Indian side.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both are true, but R is not the direct explanation for A.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true, but R does not directly explain the fertility of the Northern Plains.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

questions.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are true statements. The Northern Plains are indeed fertile (A), and the Himalayas do act as a crucial climatic barrier (R). However, the primary reason for the fertility of the Northern Plains is the deposition of rich alluvial soil by the Himalayan rivers, not directly the climatic barrier effect. The climatic barrier role influences rainfall and temperature, which indirectly supports the rivers, but it's not the direct explanation for the soil's fertility.
questions.hint: Evaluate the direct relationship between the assertion and reason.
questions.subject: icse9-sst

questions.question: Which of the following mountain ranges is considered the oldest in India and represents a highly denuded relict mountain system?

options.explanation: The Himalayas are relatively young fold mountains.
The Satpura Range is older than the Himalayas but not the oldest in India.
The Aravalli Range is one of the oldest mountain ranges in the world.
The Western Ghats are relatively younger compared to the Aravalli Range.

questions.explanation: The Aravalli Range, located in Rajasthan and extending into Gujarat, is one of the oldest fold mountain ranges in the world. Over millions of years, it has undergone significant erosion, leaving behind relict peaks.
questions.hint: This range is named after a region in Rajasthan.
questions.subject: icse9-sst

questions.question: A group of mountaineers plans to travel from the Kashmir Valley to the Kargil district in Ladakh. Which significant mountain pass would they most likely use to cross the Greater Himalayas?

options.explanation: Nathu La is located in Sikkim.
Zoji La connects the Kashmir Valley to Kargil and Leh.
Rohtang Pass is located in Himachal Pradesh.
Shipki La is located in Himachal Pradesh.

questions.explanation: Zoji La is a vital pass in the Greater Himalayas that connects the Kashmir Valley (Srinagar) to Kargil and Leh in Ladakh. Nathu La is in Sikkim, Rohtang Pass connects Kullu Valley to Lahaul and Spiti in Himachal Pradesh, and Shipki La is also in Himachal Pradesh, connecting it to Tibet.
questions.hint: This pass is located in the Greater Himalayas and connects Kashmir to Ladakh.
questions.subject: icse9-sst

questions.question: The longitudinal valleys lying between the Lesser Himalayas (Himachal) and the Shivaliks are known by local names such as 'Dehra Dun', 'Kotli Dun', and 'Patli Dun'. What is the general term for these valleys?

options.explanation: Doabs are the land between two rivers, not valleys in the Himalayas.
Duars are used for valleys in the eastern Himalayas.
Duns are the general term for these longitudinal valleys in the western Himalayas.
Gorges are deep valleys formed by rivers, not the same as Duns.

questions.explanation: These characteristic longitudinal valleys found between the Lesser Himalayas and the Shivaliks are commonly referred to as 'Duns' in the western part (e.g., Dehra Dun) and 'Duars' in the eastern part.
questions.hint: This term is used for valleys in the Himalayas.
questions.subject: icse9-sst

questions.question: Which of the given statements about the Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats are correct?

options.explanation: Statement 2 is incorrect as the Western Ghats are higher in average elevation than the Eastern Ghats.
Statement 2 is incorrect as the Western Ghats are higher in average elevation than the Eastern Ghats.
Both statements 1 and 3 are correct.
Statement 2 is incorrect as the Western Ghats are higher in average elevation than the Eastern Ghats.

questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct because the Western Ghats are continuous and can only be crossed through passes. Statement 2 is incorrect as the Western Ghats have a higher average elevation (900-1600m) compared to the Eastern Ghats (600m). Statement 3 is correct because the highest peak of the Peninsular Plateau, Anai Mudi, is located in the Western Ghats.
questions.hint: Recall the average elevations and continuity of the Western and Eastern Ghats.
questions.subject: icse9-sst

questions.question: Which of the following is the highest peak in the Indian Himalayas, located entirely within India?

options.explanation: Mount Everest is located in Nepal, not entirely within India.
Kanchenjunga is the highest peak entirely within India's political boundaries but is not the highest peak in the Indian Himalayas when considering the Karakoram Range.
Nanda Devi is a high peak in India but is lower than K2.
K2 is the highest peak in the Indian Himalayas, located in the Karakoram Range within the Gilgit-Baltistan region.

questions.explanation: While Kanchenjunga is the highest peak entirely within India's political boundaries as commonly understood for the Himalayan range proper, K2 is the highest peak in India, located in the Karakoram Range (part of the Trans-Himalayan range) in the Gilgit-Baltistan region. Mount Everest is in Nepal. Nanda Devi is also in India but lower than K2. For ICSE Class 9, K2 is often considered the highest peak in India.
questions.hint: Consider the location and range of the peaks mentioned.
questions.subject: icse9-sst

questions.question: The Great Himalayas, also known as Himadri, are characterized by:

options.explanation: The Shiwaliks are composed of unconsolidated sediments, not the Great Himalayas.

options.text: Having an average height of 3,700 to 4,500 meters.
options.explanation: This average height is characteristic of the Lesser Himalayas (Himachal), not the Great Himalayas.

options.text: Having the highest peaks with an average height of 6,000 meters.
options.explanation: The Great Himalayas are known for their highest peaks with an average height of over 6,000 meters.

options.text: Being home to famous hill stations like Shimla and Mussoorie.
options.explanation: Hill stations like Shimla and Mussoorie are located in the Lesser Himalayas (Himachal), not the Great Himalayas.

questions.explanation: The Himadri or Great Himalayas are known for their towering peaks, including Mount Everest, Kanchenjunga, etc., with an average height of over 6,000 meters. The Himachal or Lesser Himalayas have an average height of 3,700 to 4,500 meters and are known for hill stations. The Shiwaliks are composed of unconsolidated sediments.
questions.hint: Focus on the average height and features of the Great Himalayas.
questions.subject: icse9-sst

questions.question: Assertion (A): The Northern Plains of India are highly fertile and densely populated. Reason (R): The Himalayas are a source of perennial rivers that deposit rich alluvial soil in the plains.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: While both are true, R does not directly explain the dense population of the Northern Plains.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true, but R is not the direct explanation for the dense population.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true statements.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true statements.

questions.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are individually true statements. The Northern Plains are indeed fertile and densely populated. The Himalayas do give rise to perennial rivers that deposit alluvial soil. However, the reason R explains why the plains are fertile, but not directly why they are densely populated (though fertility contributes to population density, it's not the sole or direct explanation for the density itself).
questions.hint: Evaluate the relationship between the assertion and the reason.

questions.question: Which of the following mountain ranges forms the easternmost boundary of the Himalayas, bending sharply to the south and spreading along the eastern boundary of India?

options.explanation: The Pir Panjal Range is part of the Lesser Himalayas, not the easternmost boundary.
The Dhauladhar Range is part of the Lesser Himalayas, not the easternmost boundary.
The Zaskar Range is part of the Trans-Himalayas, not the easternmost boundary.
The Purvanchal Hills form the easternmost boundary of the Himalayas, bending sharply to the south.

questions.explanation: The Purvanchal Hills (or Eastern Hills and Mountains) represent the eastward extension of the Himalayas, which bend sharply to the south beyond the Dihang gorge and run along the eastern boundary of India, comprising ranges like the Patkai Bum, Naga Hills, Manipur Hills, and Mizo Hills. The other options are ranges within the main Himalayan system.
questions.hint: Consider the easternmost extension of the Himalayas.
questions.subject: icse9-sst

questions.question: A group of mountaineers planned an expedition to a region characterized by high peaks with an average elevation of 6,000 meters, prominent glacial formations, and composed of granite and gneiss. Which division of the Himalayas are they most likely exploring?

options.explanation: The Shiwaliks are the outermost range with lower elevations and unconsolidated sediments.
The Lesser Himalayas have an average elevation of 3,700 to 4,500 meters.
The Great Himalayas are characterized by high peaks, prominent glaciers, and granite and gneiss composition.
The Trans-Himalayan Range lies north of the Great Himalayas and has distinct characteristics.

questions.explanation: The characteristics provided—average elevation of 6,000 meters, prominent glaciers (like Gangotri, Yamunotri, Siachen), composition of granite and gneiss, and housing the highest peaks—are all defining features of the Great Himalayas or Himadri. The Shiwaliks are the outermost range with lower elevations and unconsolidated sediments. The Lesser Himalayas have an average elevation of 3,700 to 4,500 meters. The Trans-Himalayan Range is distinct and lies north of the Great Himalayas.
questions.hint: Analyze the given characteristics to identify the correct division of the Himalayas.
questions.subject: icse9-sst
